title: The Burning Heretic
text: A woman is tied to a stake in the square, the pyre stacked to her knees and soaked in oil. She is not praying. The Court's priests turn to you with a lit torch and smiles: it is custom, they say, for a passing noble to do the honour.

options.label: Take the torch, and light it. When in the Court, do as the Court does.

outcomes.text: She does not scream. The Court approves warmly. Far off beyond the Gate, something else approves too, hungry for more.

options.label: Cut her loose, before the flames can take her.

outcomes.text: The priests stop smiling and call their guards. The crowd will remember your faces kindly, though that may not save you.

options.label: The wisest argues that she deserves a trial, and buys her time with words.

outcomes.text: A long, dull argument delays the burning. In the night she slips her ropes and is gone.
The priests listen politely, then light it themselves. They make you watch until the end.
